Fix: the unit moved from ioChurnUnits to ioPause.cgroupPatterns in modules/nixos/services/memory-emergency-guard.nix, an edit the dead run had already made (daemon commits 7134cb3c5 + 64da0d753). This autopsy added the regression pin checks.x86_64-linux.guard-churn-listener-selftest (builds rc 0, five negative mutants fail; f0569fc80), a blocked-deploy live-verify row in docs/todo/stability.md and the closeout report (commit f362e1b20, footer last line). Proof: selftest build rc 0, nix flake check --no-build --all-systems at f362e1b20 printed all checks passed, TODO gate rc 0. NOT deployed: live gen-1032 still carries the old CHURN_UNITS (the 00:43 deploy attempt was pressure-gate refused with exit 12 and was not forced), so the check can re-alert until the next evo-x2 deploy; the unit has run uninterrupted since 02:34 because no escalation fired since. Nov 27 18:20:54 evo-x2 gatus[748029]: 2026/11/27 18:20:54 [watchdog.handleAlertsToTrigger] Sending initial discord alert because alert for endpoint=Memory Emergency Guard with description='Memory emergency guard TRIPPED (or the guard died): the machine entered a pre-freeze zone (low MemAvailable, near-full zram, PSI refault thrash, episodic memory stall, or sustained I/O stall with disk-busy corroboration) and FastFlowLM + its activation socket + the resumable I/O churn units (btrbk/balance/scrub) were force-stopped. ## pstore (EFI) crash dump and kdump capture line (read from the next boot)

systemd-pstore.service archives the EFI pstore dump of a panic at the start of the boot AFTER the crash, so this section reads the NEXT boot, not this one. With a crash image loaded the surviving dump is often the log of the CAPTURE kernel (512 MiB kernel: "N pages RAM" below 2000000), not of the main kernel: the token says whose log it is (decoded by scripts/lib/pstore-records.sh).
Records: journalctl -b <next boot> -o json SYSLOG_IDENTIFIER=systemd-pstore, the validated unprivileged selector (on systemd 262 _SYSTEMD_UNIT=systemd-pstore.service and _COMM=systemd-pstore match nothing; /var/lib/systemd/pstore and /var/crash are root-only).
kdump: the journal of the 10 min after the cut, matched on the two lines kdump-save.service prints ("kdump-save: wrote /var/crash/" = saved, "kdump-save: vmcore-dmesg FAILED" = failed; modules/nixos/services/_kdump-capture-units.nix).
An empty read is never evidence: records=0 means "that boot archived no dump", never "no crash".

## Remote log tail — ClickHouse death window (signoz_logs.distributed_logs_v2)

Death window per M22: [journal cut -> next boot], epoch-ns UTC. At a watchdog death the local journal loses its final ~30-90s to flush lag; when the OTel->ClickHouse pipeline is alive the remote tail is FRESHER than the journal cut (#36: newest row 5s before the cut), and when the collector died pre-death the pipeline is silently DARK (#37: 4h19m outage).
Window: 1795859008000000000 -> 1795859166000000000 epoch-ns UTC (2026-11-28 09:43:28 -> 2026-11-28 09:46:06 UTC)
Control window (positive control, 2026-11-26): 1795858408000000000 -> 1795859008000000000 epoch-ns UTC (2026-11-28 09:33:28 -> 2026-11-28 09:43:28 UTC), the 600 s before the cut; the verdict below rests on BOTH windows, so 0 rows after the cut alone are never read as a dead pipeline.
Verdict: alive-behind. The pipeline was alive BEFORE the journal cut: the control window (the 600 s before the cut) holds 31740 row(s), newest 1795859004905057000 = 2026-11-28 09:43:24 UTC, 3 s before the cut. The death window holds 0 rows because the remote tail is BEHIND the journal cut, so the empty window is NOT evidence of a dead pipeline (until 2026-11-26 this state was reported as a dark pipeline). ClickHouse holds nothing newer than the cut: the final flush gap of the journal is NOT covered by the remote tail for this boot.
